why: This is the light the two voxel targets were measured to be lit by, copied out of
the two files that carry it so that a change to either can be SEEN. The elevation
and the azimuth come from the direction of the lit faces in the targets, because
neither target carries a readable cast shadow; the split between sun and sky comes
from reproducing the targets' own orientation ladder through this render's tone
curve, and it puts seventy per cent of an open top face's light in the beam.
IT IS SEALED BECAUSE IT MOVES EVERYTHING AT ONCE. The meadow, the paving, the
worked stone, the rocks and the weather are all lit through these numbers, so a
session that nudges one of them to make its own crop land has moved every other
session's crop at the same time -- and the next gate reads that as a fitting error
somewhere else and fits against it. There is no session from inside which that
change can be judged, which is why the decision is the coordinator's.
tools/guards/guard-luce-sigillo.mjs compares this against what is on disk and
refuses on any drift. The coordinator takes the decision deliberately:
npm run guard:all -- --coordinator
which re-seals and says so. Commit a re-seal on its own, so the walk that approves
the new light has one change to look at.
sun.elevationRange and sun.azimuthSpread are under the seal with the two angles.
They are not the sun: they are the window the dome's optics were fitted inside, and
rewriting them without redoing that fit would falsify the record of it.
